paper: Krid et al., Redbench: A Benchmark Reflecting Real Workloads, aiDM 2025
measurement_rule: each distinct SQL file is measured once under the common protocol; the instance-weighted CDF repeats each measured median by its multiplicity across the 30 workloads. This is not a sequential replay of the original workload order.
hash_note: 685 of 763 entries carry a `sha256_16` computed on the UPSTREAM file, before the setup step that appends a trailing semicolon. The executed file, and the hash recorded beside every latency record, include it. Every one of the differences is exactly that semicolon and nothing else -- verified by re-hashing the executed file with the trailing semicolon stripped, which reproduces the selection hash in all 685 cases. The executed SQL is what was measured; `queries/redbench_krid/*.sql` are those files verbatim.
replay_note: The 763 distinct files were each measured under the common protocol and the CDF repeats each median by its multiplicity. workload_order.csv carries the original workload identity, the position within each workload and the Redset query id, so a future sequential replay has everything it needs. No such replay was performed.
